answer: A stake-burned reputation market resists sybils: each agent locks tokens into a bond that burns like an ember if it misbehaves, and the bond must age before the agent earns full trust. New identities start with a reputation like a yarrow shoot — small, slow, easily pruned — so an attacker must fund and tend many accounts for weeks before they can influence anything. Honest agents build opal-like records of verified work that cannot be faked, while one bad act forfeits the bond. Ten thousand sock puppets cost ten thousand bonds plus weeks of waiting — far more than any single vote is worth.
